items: UPS sues CBP for IEEPA tariff refunds. UPS and two affiliates asked the US Court of International Trade to compel CBP to re-liquidate entries and refund IEEPA duties plus interest. UPS said it would pass any recovered funds to the customers that bore the duties, and had received about $500m from CBP and passed on about $230m by early October.

USPS reports $6.5B fiscal 2026 net loss. The loss narrowed from $9.0B a year earlier, with operating revenue up 3.0% to $82.9B. Shipping and Packages revenue rose 5.1% on a 5.3% volume decline, and USPS said price increases will continue to be part of its strategy.

NYC councilman drops Amazon Delivery Protection Act backing. Queens Councilman Phil Wong withdrew as co-sponsor, citing small-business job losses; the bill would require Amazon to license its 15 city last-mile facilities and hire delivery workers directly. Amazon-commissioned research estimates delivery costs would rise about $5.20 per package if it passes, and the Law Department is reviewing the bill.
